draft.title: Managing debt
card: Debt is money you borrow and must pay back, usually with interest. Interest is the extra amount the lender charges for the loan.
Borrow within your means
before taking a loan, check that your income can cover the repayments as well as your other costs.
Highest interest first
keep up the minimum repayments on every debt, then put any extra money towards the debt with the highest interest rate. This cuts the total interest you pay.
Emergency savings
keep some savings for surprises, such as a car repair. Without them, you may have to borrow again, and owe more than you can manage.
draft.remember: Manage debt by borrowing only what you can repay, paying the highest interest first and saving for emergencies.

a.q: Liam has a credit card debt at a high interest rate and a car loan at a lower rate. He has some extra money each month. What should he do?
opts: Put the extra towards the credit card debt
Put the extra towards the car loan
Spread the extra evenly over both debts
Save the extra and make no extra repayments
a.why: The credit card has the higher interest rate, so extra repayments on it cut the most interest. The car loan is tempting if it is the bigger debt, but its lower rate means less interest is saved.
a.clue: Which debt costs him more for each dollar owed?

b.q: Priya earns a casual wage in Perth. She wants a new phone on credit, but the repayments would use most of her pay. Which advice best fits good debt management?
opts: Skip it, as she could not comfortably repay the loan
Take it, as she can borrow more if she runs short
Take it, as a lower interest rate means any loan is safe
Take it, as emergency savings are not needed with a loan
b.why: Borrowing only what you can repay means the repayments must fit alongside other costs. Most of her pay going to repayments leaves little room, so she should not borrow. A low interest rate does not help if she cannot afford the repayments.
b.clue: Think about whether her income can cover the repayments and her other costs.

a.best: Put the extra towards the credit card debt

b.best: Skip it, as she could not comfortably repay the loan

problems.detail: The right option is the only 'Skip it' among three 'Take it' options, and the only one with a qualifier ('comfortably'). A student could pick it as the odd one out without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card, remember line and question a are accurate and fit the point. In question b, the right answer stands out as the only 'Skip it' option with a qualifier, which makes it easy to guess.
